To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Stackelberg game between the miners and the cloud/fog service provider can be solved by using the best response strategies and that the cloud/fog pricing strategy is unique for both uniform and non-uniform pricing schemes.

the cloud/fog resource provider can maximize the total revenue by offering a unique price to all miners, and that miners with more computation resources will purchase the cloud/fog resources in proportion to their computation resources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an efficient and fair resource management mechanism that is beneficial to both the miners and the cloud/fog service providers in a blockchain network.
the resource management and pricing in the cloud/fog computing environment, where the blockchain consensus process is outsourced.
the design of a lightweight blockchain consensus protocol that is suitable for cloud/fog resource management and pricing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cloud/fog resource pricing and management for blockchain consensus is a two-stage game, which can be solved by backward induction.
, for the uniform pricing, the cloud/fogs are better off with a higher number of miners in the network.
our proposed model and the analysis can be applied to the resource management in the proof of work-based blockchains, where miners offload their computational load to the cloud/fogs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a game theoretic framework for the interaction between the miners and the cloud/fog service providers in a proof of blockchain-based consensus process, where the computation load of the miners is offloaded to cloud/fog.
we provide a new framework for the cloud/fog computing resource management in a decentralized blockchain network using a Stackelberg game theoretic approach.

the miners and cloud/fog providers would benefit by forming a symbiotic relationship in which the miners can offload their computational resources to the cloud/fogs while the cloud/fog can provide a new service to the miners and earn profits from it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cloud/fog resource providers can maximize the profit by offering the computation resources to the miners at the right price.
the miners are more likely to purchase more computing resource from the cloud/fog when the cloud/fog uses discriminatory pricing scheme.
the blockchain network can achieve higher throughput with the help of cloud/fog resources, which is a significant improvement in the performance of blockchain networks.
